bf16_reference_shards_1_to_9.recompute_cost_total: about 54 minutes of GPU to rebuild all nine

tiers.applies_to: any third-party artifact that a published number of ours cites
tiers.measured_cost: 2.34 GB of wire transfer for 149.3 GB of content across two mirrors, about 1.6 %, because Hub storage is content-addressed and the bytes already exist there
tiers.name: mirror
tiers.what_it_does_not_preserve: independent byte-level redundancy. A mirror is NOT a backup: our copy and upstream's plausibly reference the same underlying chunks. Nobody may later assume we hold physical copies we do not hold. Real redundancy is a separate decision with a real bandwidth bill and needs its own justification.
tiers.what_it_preserves: the CITATION: a resolvable repo id, revision and digest table that survive an upstream squash or delete

tiers.counter_rule: do NOT preserve when re-downloading would cost more wall-clock than re-capturing
tiers.name: preserve
tiers.rule: preserve when (a) recompute costs GPU-hours, or (b) an input has ceased to exist so it cannot be regenerated at all, or (c) it is a shared reference that many future runs replay against

tiers.name: state the recompute cost
tiers.rule: delete it freely, but any receipt that names a deleted artifact must state what recomputing it costs
tiers.worked_example: the ten-shard NVFP4 capture set: 19 captures x 10.7 GiB is about 200 GB of upload to avoid roughly 6 minutes of GPU each, so uploading is the wrong call and receipts/nvfp4-v5-measurement.json states the per-artifact cost instead

The weights are byte-identical to current upstream HEAD, but tokenizer.json and one metadata field did change, so the comparison can only be cited through the mirror.

contract: uploads the directory in one hf invocation
re-verifies every file against the remote copy at the revision the upload produced
refuses, non-zero, if any file is absent remotely, differs in size, or differs in digest
prints the delete command on success and NEVER deletes anything itself

tested.refuses_on_digest_mismatch: a same-length one-byte local edit was caught by digest comparison (git blob id), exit 1, no delete command printed
tested.refuses_on_missing_remote_file: an extra local file absent from the repo was caught, exit 1
tested.refuses_on_size_mismatch: a 43-byte local append was caught by size comparison, exit 1
tested.refuses_preflight: missing arguments, absolute or '..' dataset path, non-existent directory, unset HF_HOME, unauthenticated HF_HOME
tested.success_path: ran for real on the shard 1-9 suite views: 108 files, 5,188,488 B, all 108 re-downloaded and sha256-matched under --deep, delete command printed, local directory still present afterwards (revision 0a45aeae31d38ad0742703ac4505d24ebd26fe01)

tool.why_it_does_not_delete: a tool that both publishes and deletes will eventually delete after a publish that only looked successful. The delete stays a separate, human-run step.

verification.honest_statement_of_strength: 5326 of 5835 files (157,456,484 B) were re-downloaded and re-hashed end to end. The remaining 509 files (10,669,340,384 B, the 10 GB hidden-state tree) were verified by comparing the Hub's own LFS sha256 and byte size against the local values; re-downloading all 10 GB to re-hash it was judged impractical, so three of those 512 files were additionally pulled from the CDN and re-hashed as a spot check, and all 512 were separately confirmed against the digests the capture tool itself recorded in capture-manifest.json.
verification.independent_cross_check: All 512 hidden_NNNN.safetensors local digests were compared with the per-file sha256 the capture tool recorded in capture-manifest.json at capture time: 512/512 match, and the manifest's complete flag is true. The tree published is therefore the tree that was captured, not merely a self-consistent copy of whatever was on disk.

kinds.remote_sha256_lfs_oid: the Hub stores this file in LFS and reports its sha256 as the LFS oid; that remote sha256 was compared with the local sha256, and the remote size with the local size. This is an end-to-end content check over the full bytes, but the digest is one the Hub computed - these bytes were NOT re-downloaded and re-hashed here.
kinds.served_sha256_readback: the file was re-downloaded from the Hub and its sha256 recomputed from the received bytes, then compared with the local sha256. Strongest available check: it proves what the CDN actually serves.
kinds.served_sha256_readback_lfs_spot: same check, applied to a sample of the LFS tree spread across its start, middle and end rather than a prefix.

verification.principle: Every uploaded file was re-verified against the remote copy after upload, the way the model-card uploads are: compare a digest the Hub computed over the bytes it stored against the same digest computed over the local bytes. Strength is reported per file rather than averaged, so no check is implied that was not performed.

why_this_receipt_exists: The v5 KLD ladder captured six models per 512-context shard, verified the reports, then deleted that shard's hidden states to make room for the next shard - ten times. The reports survived; roughly 190 GB of reusable capture did not, and a later cross-engine run had to re-download tens of GB of GGUF and re-capture hidden states that had existed and been thrown away. Recompute is slower than download and needs a GPU that is usually busy. Publishing the inputs also doubles as transparency. This receipt is the honest cost of the old habit and the justification for the new policy.
